headline: All majors underwater on the 200-day; funding expensive and longs crowded; whales moving coins onto exchanges while ETF flows split.
paragraphs: The regime is bear. Every asset in the major seven sits below its 200-day simple moving average, and not one has triggered a golden cross. Bitcoin at 63,371, down 49.2% from its 12-month high of 124,739, anchors the frame. Ethereum at 1,883 is 60.9% off its high. Solana has fallen 69.2%, XRP 69.3%, Cardano 81.1% from peak. These are not corrections within a bull trend; they are assets grinding lower through long-term averages. Bitcoin's RSI sits at 45.2, Ethereum at 51.6, both neutral leaning soft. Solana's RSI at 54.4 is the only one approaching overbought territory among the majors. The single bright spot for momentum is the MACD cross: Solana, BNB, and Doge all show MACD above signal line, a sign that short-term momentum is inflecting up. BTC and ETH remain below signal. This is not a full confirmation of trend reversal; it is a small disagreement between the daily structure (down) and the 8-bar momentum (up). That divergence is the only tension in favor of a reversal candidate.

Positioning on the leverage markets tells a story of crowded long bets and expensive carry. Bitcoin funding on OKX runs at 0.01% per eight hours, annualizing to 11% annually, well above the baseline cost of capital. Ethereum matches it. The long-to-short ratio on Bitcoin is 1.87, on Ethereum 1.8, and on Solana 2.15. XRP is at 3.39 longs per short, and Doge at 5.29, extreme imbalance. Open interest remains substantial: Bitcoin alone sits on 2.06 billion in notional exposure, Ethereum on 1.33 billion. Over the last 24 hours, liquidations have struck heavily on the long side, with Bitcoin longs liquidated for 5.68 million against shorts for 2.65 million, and Ethereum longs for 8.7 million against shorts for 3.17 million. Funding is paying longs to hold, and longs are the crowded side. When funding is this high and the long book this full, the market is pricing conviction and exposure. Any break lower clears overstretched positions.

Flows paint a mixed picture. Bitcoin spot ETF flows show a 3.6 million outflow on 13 Aug, the most recent session, with outflows persisting over the last five sessions to a cumulative negative 99.8 million, same direction for two days. Ethereum ETF flows point the opposite direction: inflows of 6.5 million on 13 Aug, and cumulative inflows of 47.2 million over the last five sessions, also same direction for two days. The traditional-finance bid is not uniform. Stablecoin float sits at 306.4 billion, flat on a 30-day view at minus 0.58%, neither building nor draining meaningfully. Whale activity over the last 48 hours shows 262.8 million in Bitcoin moving net onto exchanges, with the largest single moves being 127.5 million into Coinbase Institutional and 117.4 million into Binance. Offsetting that, 70.6 million and 51.6 million left Coinbase Institutional. The weekly net trend is volatile, swinging from minus 812.9 million to plus 1.29 billion week to week, a sign the large player base is trading rather than holding conviction in one direction.

The Fear and Greed gauge stands at 29, deep in Fear territory, anchored in the recent 30-day range of 25 to 33. This is not capitulation extreme, but it reflects the sustained pressure and the distance from supply-side demand. Sentiment and tape are not far apart on the day-to-day: prices are soft, leverage is crowded and expensive, and whales are rotating into exchange inventories. The contradiction worth watching is between the structural position (all below 200-day) and the derivative signal (funding high, longs full, but some assets showing MACD momentum crosses). If Bitcoin reclaims its 200-day moving average, that would be the first structural break in regime. If funding flips negative or the long-to-short ratios compress sharply, the leverage excess would unwind. If whale net flow reverses to outflow (coins moving off exchanges) while funding remains high, that would signal conviction from large holders that a bottom is near. None of those have happened yet. For now, the tape shows a market that is overleveraged on the long side in a downtrend, with traditional finance buying Ethereum but selling Bitcoin, and large traders treating this as a trading range rather than a directional setup.
